correctness.rationale: Signed-jump representation integrates J_s against Df and does not charge boundary traces. For each jump the L1 residual is twice the kernel crossing mass. From the stated image identity F_t(s)=integral_0^s p_t(s,y)dy is simply integral_0^{2s} N_t(z)dz. The half-period mass integral_0^1 N_t is 1/2 and N_t>0, so E_t'(s)=2(1-2F_t(s)) has strictly positive sign left of 1/2 and strictly negative sign right of it. This also avoids relying on weak point-mass convergence alone for the half-mass limit at its atom. Equality in the BV bound forces |Df| to concentrate on the midpoint. Integrating the cosine eigenfunctions over opposite sides of the jump gives the stated odd-mode series; differentiating proves the strict time signs. Poisson summation of the odd Gaussian series gives the alternating image sum for C'(t); integrating the first image error uses integral_0^t u^-1/2 exp(-1/(4u))du=O(t^(3/2)exp(-1/(4t))). The next odd eigenmode gives the stated long-time remainder. The frozen checker was inspected, not run. The independent check passed six comparisons of the image first moment with the odd-mode series.
residual_risks: The proof concerns the specified Neumann generator and interior variation, not trace-charged BV or other boundary conditions.
